memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the Gadites, according to their clans. This is what Moses had given to the half-tribe of Manasseh, that is, to half the family of the descendants of Manasseh, according to its clans: The territory extending from Mahanaim and including all of Bashan, the entire realm of Og king of Bashan—all the settlements of Jair in Bashan, sixty towns, half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei (the royal cities of Og in Bashan). This was for the descendants of Makir son of Manasseh—for half of the sons of Makir, according to their clans - Josh 13:28-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The half-tribe of Manasseh receives its inheritance — Bashan, sixty towns, the former realm of the giant king Og. Manasseh was one of Joseph's sons, and this tribe would be split, with half settling east of the Jordan and half to the west. Even a divided tribe was carefully given its due portion.

It is worth pausing on the phrase "sixty towns." What was once Og's kingdom of terror is now a settled inheritance of sixty peaceful communities for God's people. The ground that had belonged to a giant now belongs to families building homes and raising children. This is what God does — He takes territory once held by what frightened us and turns it into a place of belonging and blessing.

Think of what that means for the hard places in your own story. The very ground where you once faced a giant — a fear, a season of struggle, a battle you thought would destroy you — God is able to transform into settled, fruitful ground. He does not merely help us survive our giants; He gives us to dwell in peace where they once ruled. The kingdom of Og became the home of Manasseh, and the places of our old battles can, by God's grace, become places of rest and fruitfulness in Him (Isa 61:3).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What former "kingdom of Og" in your life might God be turning into settled ground?
- Do you believe God can make a place of peace where you once faced a giant?
- How does God's habit of transforming hard ground give you hope today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You turn the ground of old battles into places of peace. Where I once faced giants, give me rest and fruitfulness by Your grace. Amen.
